findings.how_to_check: Run 'python replication/check_claims.py' and observe 21 UNCHECKED claims; search the repo for model training code ('git ls-files | Select-String py') to confirm no training or inference scripts exist.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the model training, inference, and evaluation scripts (including checkpoint weights and dependency environments) to the repository or link an archived repository containing the code that generates merged_data.dta and Table 1.
findings.title: Machine learning transcription and evaluation pipeline is entirely absent from the repository
findings.what_the_code_does: The replication package registers Table 1 accuracies, Table A1 hyperparameters, training sample counts, GPU benchmarks, and per-state model transcription files as 'nocode' (UNCHECKED). No Python or Stata code in the repository trains the neural networks, crops images, runs inference, or evaluates sequence/token accuracy.
findings.why_it_matters: The core empirical contribution of the paper cannot be reproduced or audited from source; a journal data editor or referee cannot verify Table 1 or how the machine transcriptions were generated.

findings.how_to_check: Run 'stata -b do replication/config.do' on any computer whose hostname is not ARTS-ECON-CM or ARTS-ECON-SHSRV; it halts with r(198) at line 40.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace hardcoded hostname checks in config.do with configurable base-path globals or environment variables, remove hostname exit checks in hash scripts, pass --paper-repo dynamically in PowerShell runners, and make Stata executable paths configurable.
findings.title: Machine-specific hostname gating and hardcoded drive paths prevent execution in external environments
findings.what_the_code_does: config.do checks c(hostname) against 'ARTS-ECON-CM' and 'ARTS-ECON-SHSRV' and throws error 198 on any other machine. hash_inputs.py, hash_inputs_machineB.py, and check_claims.py also exit immediately if the hostname does not match. run_machineA.do and run_machineB.do hardcode absolute paths 'D:/repos/...' and 'F:/github_repos/...'. Run-Stata.ps1 hardcodes 'C:\Program Files (x86)\Stata15\StataMP-64.exe'.
findings.why_it_matters: An external replicator cannot run preflights, manifest checks, or do-files without modifying configuration files and script headers.

findings.how_to_check: Tabulate in validation_by_link_status.do or deaglan_abe_jw.tex whether the links verified correct by the genealogical truth set are disproportionately those where the ML transcription agrees with FamilySearch against Ancestry.
findings.suggested_fix: Disclose and discuss the shared FamilySearch provenance in Section 4.2, report sensitivity of validation rates to FamilySearch agreement, and benchmark against a non-FamilySearch ground truth where feasible.
findings.title: Genealogical truth set shares FamilySearch provenance with model's dominant agreement source
findings.what_the_code_does: The paper validates link quality against mlp_training1930_1940.dta derived from FamilySearch genealogical trees, while Section 3 notes the model agrees with FamilySearch 52% of the time vs 14% with Ancestry on discordant records.
findings.why_it_matters: Because FamilySearch user trees frequently rely on FamilySearch's transcription index, an ML transcription that strongly aligns with FamilySearch will mechanically validate at higher rates against FamilySearch trees, confounding genuine match quality with shared source errors.

findings.how_to_check: Check replication/README.md lines 258-264 ('What is not covered', item 3); search the codebase for the scripts creating link1930_1940_ans_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta.
findings.suggested_fix: Include the enum_date linkage generation code in the repository or provide a self-contained script producing the link files and middle-initial variables from cleaned input datasets.
findings.title: Core census linkage files and middle-initial variables originate from external unversioned codebase
findings.what_the_code_does: The analysis relies on pre-built intermediate files link1930_1940_{ans,true}_cleaned_noraceblock0.dta from the external 'enum_date' project, which also assigned different middle initials (Ancestry vs ML) to the old and new files.
findings.why_it_matters: Tables 2-4, Figures 3-4, and the 65% to 84% validation result depend directly on link files that cannot be generated or inspected within this repository.

findings.how_to_check: Compare \mOneUsingMalesTen (4,310,632) in replication/results/size_merges.tex with the difference between 55,347,491 and 51,036,859 in DHTS-2026-10-12.tex:399-401.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify the sample construction text in Section 3.1 to state that 4,310,632 males 10+ were excluded because they failed the cross-source transcription merge or lacked valid name/age fields.
findings.title: Draft attributes sample loss solely to name and age filters without disclosing upstream merge attrition
findings.what_the_code_does: The draft presents the reduction from 55,347,491 to 51,036,859 males 10+ as simply requiring all four name fields and non-missing age, but size_merge_outcomes.do shows the 4,310,632 gap includes census extract records that never matched into the labeled transcription dataset.
findings.why_it_matters: A referee evaluating sample selection cannot distinguish attrition caused by name/age filtering from records omitted during the upstream Ancestry-FamilySearch merge.

findings.how_to_check: Inspect replication/Run-MachineA.ps1 line 55 and Run-MachineB.ps1 line 63; compare with line 62 of Run-MachineA.ps1 which passes '--paper-repo $paper'.
findings.suggested_fix: Update line 55 of Run-MachineA.ps1 to 'python (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "check_claims.py") --paper-repo $paper' and line 63 of Run-MachineB.ps1 similarly.
findings.title: PowerShell automation drivers invoke claim checker without passing configured paper repository path
findings.what_the_code_does: Run-MachineA.ps1 defines $paper at line 28 but runs check_claims.py at line 55 without '--paper-repo $paper', causing check_claims.py to ignore the variable and fall back to claims.toml's hostname dictionary.
findings.why_it_matters: If a user overrides $paper or executes the driver on a system with a different directory layout, compare_figures.py uses $paper but check_claims.py checks the hardcoded claims.toml path or crashes.

review_limits: Runtime constraints prevented executing the full multi-hour pipeline (run_machineA.do 170 min, run_machineB.do 234 min); assessment relies on static code analysis and frozen diagnostic logs.
Raw census datasets (120+ GB restricted IPUMS full count, FamilySearch scrapes, BUNMD mortality files) are gitignored external files and could not be independently inspected or re-extracted.
Machine B linkage algorithms (ABE/JW matching and IPUMS HLINK matching) are pre-computed in external files; only table aggregation code was reviewable.
The machine learning training, inference, and image-segmentation pipelines are not in this repository and could not be evaluated.
summary: The replication package provides an exceptionally rigorous verification harness for the Stata analysis and exhibit generation tiers, with 54 draft claims programmatically verified against source outputs. However, the package cannot be executed by independent researchers due to hardcoded hostname locks and local disk paths, and it omits the machine learning pipeline that produced Table 1 and the underlying model transcriptions. The most critical fix prior to submission is eliminating the hostname gating in config.do and archiving the ML training and evaluation code.
